text:
maria: quick idea to discuss 1 bandwidth-aware offload scheduler for host<->GPU transfers.
maria: current eviction is purely hotness-driven; that can cause big PCIe floods that block small interactive evicts. propose factoring estimated transfer size and urgency into scheduling.
jun: love the goal. interactive tail matters a lot. how intrusive is this to the allocator interface?
sashank: biggest risk is fairness across tenants. if we always favor tiny interactive transfers we might starve batch tenants for throughput. need per-tenant budgets.
maria: suggested design: allocator emits lightweight hints (urgency, estimated_bytes, allow_prefetch). runtime implements a transfer scheduler that enforces urgency buckets + token-bucket bandwidth windows per tenant/pool.
olivia: so allocator still controls placement/residency but runtime controls when transfers happen. keeps allocation API small.
alex: minimal POC: implement per-tenant bandwidth gates + an "interactive" boolean on transfer submissions. No reweighting of hotness yet. This gets most benefit quickly.
jun: agree, but we need telemetry first: pcie_bytes_inflight, queued_transfers_by_urgency, avg_transfer_size_by_tenant, p99_offload_latency. otherwise tuning windows is blind.
sashank: tradeoff: coalescing/flighting transfers improves throughput but raises p99 for urgent items. scheduler must avoid coalescing interactive items with large batch drains.
maria: draft API sketch to include in RFC:

AllocHint: "urgency" (interactive|normal|batch), "estimated_bytes", "allow_prefetch"
Runtime config: per-tenant windows like {tenant: {window_bytes: 200000000, refill_ms: 1000}}

olivia: test plan: microbench mixed traffic: seq64 interactive 40% + seq2048 batch 60%; sweep window sizes and measure 95/99 latency and throughput. I can prototype a 48-hour spike.
jun: perf runner example: ./perf.sh --profile offload-sched --pattern mixed --iters 5000
sashank: topology note: CPU NUMA and PCIe switches change effective bandwidth and contention. runtime should annotate estimated cost with topology multiplier (use hwloc or sysfs probe).
maria: yes, runtime should query topology once at startup and apply cost multipliers per path.
alex: also watch kernel efficiency: we lose some compute batching benefits if we preempt large transfers too aggressively. include a compute-vs-transfer cost term in scheduling model later.
maria: proposed incremental roadmap: (1) add AllocHint struct to allocator API (urgency + size), (2) add telemetry hooks (jun), (3) simple tenant token-buckets + interactive flag gate (alex POC), (4) olivia microbench prototype, (5) topology probe helper (sashank), (6) RFC writeup.
olivia: I'll aim for a 2-day spike to get numbers and a draft microbench harness.
sashank: i'll drop a small sysfs/hwloc helper snippet into the RFC repo.
deploy-bot: canary pipeline triggered: infra-experiments/offload-sched-probe (no-prod).
maria: thanks all. please add short bullets to the RFC PR when you have prototypes so i can synthesize. :rocket:
